proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true lag varies across weeks/splits (nonstationary delay), a fixed 1-week delay can misalign peaks and cause phase errors in rolling windows.
proposals.rationale: Primary anchored template: SEIRS supports waning immunity/seasonal recycling while keeping structure minimal; a 1-week delayed_I aligns with the consistent short reporting/admission lag signal and has shown best rolling robustness.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Often reacts too quickly, producing premature rise/peak timing and degraded rolling generalization when a systematic 1-week lag is present.
proposals.rationale: Ablation to confirm delay sensitivity: same parsimonious SEIRS backbone but no observation lag, testing whether the series occasionally behaves like near-contemporaneous I-proxy reporting.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Can overshift/oversmooth dynamics, delaying peaks and underestimating early growth, which tends to hurt rolling performance when the true lag is closer to 1 week.
proposals.rationale: Neighbor ablation around the preferred delay: tests whether a slightly longer lag better matches admission timing in some splits without changing transmission structure.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Systematic phase mismatch if hospitalizations lag infections; may fit amplitude but miss peak timing and degrade under rolling splits.
proposals.rationale: Minimal non-delayed baseline within the same structure family to assess whether the delayed observation mapping is essential versus SEIRS alone capturing timing adequately.
